page: Amazon Web Services m4.2xlarge is a general purpose instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.4 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES, and FMA, but lacking AVX-512 extensions. The server is allocated 32.0 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB per core. It includes no local instance storage and relies entirely on networked volumes, while providing a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reflect the older Broadwell-generation architecture. In compute benchmarks, the instance achieves 7007.9 on PassMark CPU score and 6290.33 in stress-ng multi-core testing, positioning it in the middle 50% for multi-threaded capacity. However, single-threaded processing reflects architectural age, scoring 973.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1263.99 on stress-ng single-core, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory throughput remains stable, recording 46.46 GB/sec for uncached read-only transfers and 34.84 GB/sec for large block writes. Application metrics show 2.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.25 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced footprint for legacy enterprise deployments, background task workers, mid-tier application hosting, and moderate relational databases. Because local storage is absent and baseline networking is limited to 1 Gbps, throughput-heavy network operations or IOPS-intensive disk workloads face performance constraints. From a resource perspective, the hardware offers functional memory capacity but lower per-core efficiency compared to newer instance generations.
description: Amazon Web Services m4.2xlarge is a general purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores running at 2.4 GHz on the Xen hypervisor. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual CPU, but contains no local storage and includes a 1 Gbps baseline network interface without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance registers in the middle 50% for multi-core compute with a PassMark CPU score of 7007.9, while single-threaded tasks fall into the bottom 25% due to older microarchitecture limitations. Memory operations show uncached reads of 46.46 GB/sec. The instance serves standard business application tiers, background processing jobs, and moderate database workloads where high per-core performance, local NVMe capacity, or advanced vector processing instructions are not required.

tagline: Legacy general-purpose instance delivering eight virtual cores, thirty-two gigabytes of memory, and steady multi-threaded execution for standard enterprise applications.
